content:
Mexico's Foreign Ministry has now formally answered Texas' claim to nine Rio Grande islands: the border cannot be changed by a state government acting alone, the ministry said in a statement reported October 30–31.

The Secretariat of Foreign Affairs (SRE) said international limits are set by treaty, not by a state authority. Under the 1970 Treaty of Limits, where the Rio Grande serves as the natural border, the boundary follows the center of the river's normal channel — and that line determines sovereignty on either side, according to the ministry.

The ministry said the International Boundary and Water Commission (CILA), the binational body, is the authority empowered to apply the treaty and determine on which side of the boundary each island lies. It also warned that, under the treaty, neither country may build works that, in CILA's judgment, could divert or obstruct the river's normal flow.

The islands at issue sit in the border corridor near Laredo, Rio Bravo and El Cenizo, across from Nuevo Laredo, according to reporting on the statement. Texas Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham announced October 26 that the nine islands, totaling about 66 acres out of 28 islands reviewed at U.S. Customs and Border Protection's request, belong to Texas and could be patrolled and cleared by state forces. Buckingham has acknowledged that no criminal activity has been confirmed on these nine islands, according to the reports.

Mexico said it will closely follow any action in the area and reiterated its commitment to the treaties governing the shared border and to bilateral dialogue through established mechanisms.

This follows Webb Watch 956's earlier report on Texas' island claim; the SRE statement is the Mexican government's formal response to it.

Sources:

  • La Jornada via Mexico Solidarity Media, "Mexico's Foreign Secretariat Responds to Texas: The Border on the Río Bravo Cannot Be Modified by a State Government," October 30, 2026
  • El Vigía, "SRE advierte que Texas no puede modificar la frontera con México por decisión unilateral," October 31, 2026

title: Mexico formally answers Texas island claim: border cannot be changed by a state alone
